title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 12 (What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting)

content.overview: Section 12 provides that a person is said to be of sound mind for the purpose of making a contract if, at the time when he makes it, he is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests. A person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, may make a contract when he is of sound mind. A person who is usually of sound mind, but occasionally of unsound mind, may not make a contract when he is of unsound mind.
content.glance: Sound mind = understand the contract + form rational judgment as to its effect; test at the time of contracting; lucid intervals count.
content.study: Sound mind for contracting means capacity, at the time of making the contract, to understand it and to form a rational judgment as to its effect upon one’s interests. A person usually of unsound mind may contract in a lucid interval; a person usually of sound mind may not contract while of unsound mind. Current-law framing: fix the time of contracting; apply the understand-and-rational-judgment test; apply the usual/occasional rules.

sections.heading: Test of sound mind
sections.body: Capable of understanding the contract and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests, at the time of making it.

sections.heading: Usually unsound, occasionally sound
sections.body: May make a contract when of sound mind (lucid interval).

sections.heading: Usually sound, occasionally unsound
sections.body: May not make a contract when of unsound mind.

provisions.title: What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting

examples.title: Lucid interval
examples.body: A person usually of unsound mind contracts during a lucid interval when capable of understanding and rational judgment — competent under s. 12.

hypotheticals.question: Is mental illness alone enough to avoid every contract?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The test is capacity at the time of making the contract to understand it and form a rational judgment as to its effect.

misconceptions.trap: Any diagnosis of mental illness voids all contracts of that person.
misconceptions.correction: Section 12 tests capacity at the time of contracting; lucid intervals can support a valid contract.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 12 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Fix the time of contracting. II. Apply understand + rational judgment test. III. Apply usual/occasional rules. IV. Conclude.
